items.title: Load and peek at data
items.body:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
df.head()
df.info()                 # dtypes and non-null counts
df.describe()             # numeric summary
df.shape                  # (rows, columns)
items.description: Read a CSV and inspect it.

items.title: Read other formats
items.body:
pd.read_csv("data.csv", sep=";", encoding="utf-8", na_values=["NA", "?"], parse_dates=["date"])
pd.read_excel("data.xlsx", sheet_name="Sheet1")
pd.read_json("data.json")
pd.read_parquet("data.parquet")
pd.read_sql("SELECT * FROM t", connection)
items.description: Excel, JSON, SQL, Parquet and options for messy CSVs.

items.title: Select columns and rows
items.body:
df["age"]                      # one column (Series)
df[["name", "age"]]            # several columns (DataFrame)
df.loc[0:5, "name"]            # label-based, inclusive end
df.iloc[0:5, 0:2]              # position-based, exclusive end
df.loc[df["age"] > 30, ["name", "age"]]
items.description: [] for columns, loc by label, iloc by position.

items.title: Filter rows
items.body:
df[df["age"] > 30]
df[(df["age"] > 30) & (df["city"] == "Oslo")]       # use & | ~ with parentheses
df[df["city"].isin(["Oslo", "Rome"])]
df.query("age > 30 and city == 'Oslo'")
df[df["name"].str.contains("ad", case=False, na=False)]

items.title: Sort, rename, drop
items.body:
df.sort_values("age", ascending=False)
df.sort_values(["city", "age"])
df.rename(columns={"old": "new"})
df.drop(columns=["unused"])
df.drop_duplicates(subset=["email"])

items.title: Add and transform columns
items.body:
import numpy as np

df["age_next"] = df["age"] + 1
df["adult"] = np.where(df["age"] >= 18, "yes", "no")
df["name_len"] = df["name"].str.len()
df["clean"] = df["name"].str.strip().str.lower()
df["bucket"] = pd.cut(df["age"], bins=[0, 18, 65, 120], labels=["child", "adult", "senior"])

items.title: merge (join) DataFrames
items.body:
pd.merge(orders, customers, on="customer_id", how="left")       # inner | left | right | outer
pd.merge(a, b, left_on="id", right_on="user_id")
pd.concat([df1, df2], ignore_index=True)                       # stack rows
pd.concat([df1, df2], axis=1)                                  # side by side

items.title: Missing values
items.body:
df.isna().sum()                           # missing per column
df.dropna()                               # drop rows with any NaN
df.dropna(subset=["age"])
df["age"] = df["age"].fillna(df["age"].median())
df["city"] = df["city"].fillna("unknown")

items.title: Types and dates
items.body:
df["age"] = df["age"].astype(int)
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"], errors="coerce")
df["year"] = df["date"].dt.year
df["weekday"] = df["date"].dt.day_name()
df["category"] = df["category"].astype("category")
items.description: Convert columns and use the .dt accessor.

items.title: value_counts and pivot_table
items.body:
df["city"].value_counts()
df["city"].value_counts(normalize=True)           # proportions
pd.pivot_table(df, values="salary", index="city", columns="team", aggfunc="mean", fill_value=0)
pd.crosstab(df["city"], df["team"])

items.title: Correlation and outliers
items.body:
df.corr(numeric_only=True)
q1, q3 = df["salary"].quantile([0.25, 0.75])
iqr = q3 - q1
outliers = df[(df["salary"] < q1 - 1.5 * iqr) | (df["salary"] > q3 + 1.5 * iqr)]

items.title: NumPy: create arrays
items.body:
import numpy as np

np.array([1, 2, 3])
np.zeros((2, 3)); np.ones(4); np.eye(3)
np.arange(0, 10, 2)            # 0 2 4 6 8
np.linspace(0, 1, 5)           # 5 evenly spaced points
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
rng.random((2, 2)); rng.integers(0, 10, size=5); rng.normal(0, 1, 100)

items.title: NumPy: shape and reshape
items.body:
a = np.arange(12)
a.shape                     # (12,)
a.reshape(3, 4)
a.reshape(-1, 2)            # -1 = infer
a.T                         # transpose
a.ravel()                   # flatten

items.title: NumPy: axis operations
items.body:
m = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
m.sum(axis=0)       # [5 7 9]  per column
m.mean(axis=1)      # [2. 5.]  per row
m.max(); m.argmax(); np.std(m)
items.description: axis=0 goes down the rows (per column); axis=1 goes across (per row).

items.title: NumPy: masks and broadcasting
items.body:
a = np.array([1, 5, 10, 15])
a[a > 5]                             # [10 15]
np.where(a > 5, "big", "small")
col = np.array([[1], [2], [3]])      # shape (3, 1)
row = np.array([10, 20, 30])         # shape (3,)
col + row                            # broadcasts to (3, 3)
items.description: Filter without loops; combine arrays of different shapes.

items.title: NumPy: linear algebra
items.body:
A = np.array([[2, 1], [1, 3]])
b = np.array([1, 2])
A @ A                       # matrix product
np.linalg.inv(A)
np.linalg.solve(A, b)       # preferred over inv(A) @ b
np.linalg.eig(A)
items.description: Matrix product, inverse and solving systems.
